Artist / Group / Collective / Organizer: Amaanatdaari (Project Curators: Emad Anoushirvani, Mohsen Jafaripour)

Location.text: Amaanatdaari Space (Rasht), Bazar Art Books (Didar Gallery, Tehran)

Year / Time Period.text: Nowrouz 1403 - Rasht (March 2023) Nowrouz 1404 - Rasht (March 2024) Bazar Art Books 2025 - Didar Art Gallery (October 2025)

sections.title: Introduction
paragraphs: The Amaanatdaari�s Printing Machine was a simple and efficient mechanical device placed in the outdoor area of the Amaanatdaari Space in the Saadi Bazaar of Rasht, Guilan Province, during the Nowruz holidays. It was accessible to audiences and passersby at any hour of the day or night. The project consisted of four machines, each printing one color, allowing the participant to ultimately receive a four-color image printed all by themselves.

The machines were designed, built, and placed outdoors without the presence of project staff to allow for unmediated interaction with the audience. The project ran continuously 24/7 for 15 days. Usage instructions stated that participants could print on any surface they had with them, such as paper, books, or banknotes, as "Eidi" (New Year Gifts). In some cases, Eidi was provided to the audience to facilitate the experience. This project gradually became a recurring tradition during Nowruz, with audiences looking forward to new editions each year.
In each edition, different artists collaborated on various sections:
Nowruz 2024: Titled "Reproduce the Plain" (Dasht ra Takisir Konid), featuring artists Aysa Rashid, Kavosh Zhaleh, Mitra Soltani, and Malahat Moheb-khah, with stamp image design by Kamand Samimi.

Nowruz 2025: Titled "This One was Birth, That One was Wind" (In Yeki Zad Bud, An Yeki Bad), featuring illustrations by Yasi Mossadegh, focusing on the duality of "birth" and "wind" and the relationship between individual and collective growth.

October 2025: Amaanatdaari presented "Printing Machine No. 3" at the "Bazar Art Books 2025" (Didar Gallery), inviting Amirali Ghasemi to address themes such as the national language, the right to learn the mother tongue, preservation of linguistic cultures, and resistance against assimilation into the dominant languages. The operation manual for this part was prepared by Saba Hassanzadeh and Katayoun Masoudi.

sections.title: Context & Site
paragraphs: The project was executed in the outdoor space of Amaanatdaari within an urban context. It was presented during Nowruz at the Saadi Bazaar in Rasht and at the Bazar Art Books, an artist book fair in Tehran. This context was chosen because of the similarity between the experimental atmosphere of the book fair and the natural habitat of the project in Rasht, as well as the large audience reception in the fair.

sections.title: Motivations & Questions
paragraphs: The initial motivation stemmed from Amaanatdaari's unique location in a bazaar near Rasht's Municipality (Shahrdari) Square� a popular area filled with people and tourists during Nowruz. Its proximity to one of the few public restrooms in the area meant many people passed by simply to use that facility without necessarily intending to engage with the space.

The main design challenge was to create a project that could attract attention and provide a short, optional experience without disrupting the daily routine of the passersby. Consequently, the idea of a 24-hour machine was developed to allow direct participation without the need for a human facilitator. Other motivations included a desire to be present in urban spaces rather than enclosed galleries, which were felt to be less dynamic for this type of encounter. The project sought to bridge the gap between the visual arts and the daily lives of the public, removing physical and symbolic boundaries to allow anyone to enter an artistic experience at any time without prior preparation.

sections.title: Constraints & Strategies
paragraphs: The most significant constraint was the lack of financial support, which impacted development and maintenance. Additionally, because the machines were in public spaces and used constantly, they occasionally suffered damage or malfunctions. In response, the project emphasized simplicity in design and the ease of reproduction and repair. The simple mechanical mechanism allowed the project to continue despite wear and tear or improper use. Furthermore, Amaanatdaari functioned as a small, independent structure�a strategy that allowed for high-standard execution on a limited scale.

sections.title: Fundings & Partners
paragraphs: Financial Supporters: The project is self-funded by Amaanatdaari in Rasht. During the participation at Bazar Art Books 2025, posters and prints were offered in exchange for a small contribution by the visitor to cover the cost of shipping and production.

sections.title: About the Artist
paragraphs: Amaanatdaari is an independent, artist-run space located in one of the local bazaars of Rasht. It has been active for over two years, focusing on exhibiting alternative and experimental projects. Website/Telegram:

The primary audience consisted of everyone passing by Amaanatdaari during the execution periods (the New Year holidays) whose attention was drawn to the machine. The entire printing process was performed by the participants, who played an active role�from selecting the printing surface to operating the machine and executing the various steps. A core objective of the project was to facilitate the unmediated presence of the audience, removing any physical distance between the public and the art piece (by eliminating even the thin glass of a vitrine).
